潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Xinxiang Yin, Xinglang Zhang, Haodong Chen, Zhiqing Cui, Weidong Tang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper presents Anchor, a self-evolving agent that optimizes memory retention through source decision testing, enhancing performance in long-horizon tasks by up to 19.9%.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces Mega-MMDF, a comprehensive dataset for multimodal deepfake detection, and DeepfakeBench-MM, a standardized evaluation framework, enhancing detector performance across diverse forgery pipelines.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.

潘佳老师实验室.title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Zunhai Su, Keyu Fan, Ruishan Guo, Zhongzhu Zhou, Jingzehua Xu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: QuantStream3D introduces a novel KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers, achieving significant accuracy and efficiency improvements through geometry-guided mixed-precision techniques.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch. Quantization sensitivity varies across precision choices and cache locations, while perturbed retrieval changes geometry-head inputs and propagates through subsequent predictions and KV writes. Guided by these findings, we propose QuantStream3D, to our knowledge the first dedicated KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers. Geometry-Guided Mixed-Precision KV Quantization protects sensitive cross-view evidence, while Geometry-Aligned Quantization-Aware Distillation jointly adapts transformer blocks and geometry heads on student-generated quantized history. Across five benchmarks and two backbones, QuantStream3D achieves near-lossless geometric accuracy in most settings with predominantly 2-bit KV caches, and many configurations surpass unquantized inference. Compared with LLM-oriented KV quantizers, it reduces TUM absolute trajectory error and NeuralRGBD completeness error by up to 57.4% and 69.7%, respectively. Integration with existing native cache-pruning methods further pushes compression while improving reconstruction quality on NeuralRGBD. Our optimized StreamVGGT backend achieves $5.05\times$ physical KV compression and 23.1% lower latency at batch size one. Under a fixed memory budget on the same GPU, it supports $5.4\times$ the maximum batch size and up to $1.67\times$ the peak throughput of unquantized inference. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be made publicly available.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Generalist Action Critic: Harnessing Frontier Models in Autonomous Driving
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yun Yan, Shizhi Hu, Zhichao Li, Yang Guan, Shiqi Liu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The Generalist Action Critic (GAC) framework enhances autonomous driving safety and performance by integrating frontier models with specialized planners for trajectory assessment and reselection.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Frontier models have demonstrated remarkable general-purpose reasoning capabilities, opening new possibilities for intelligent decision making in the physical world. In autonomous driving, many recent approaches seek to leverage these capabilities through additional adaptation for action output, particularly in scenarios where existing models underperform. We introduce Generalist Action Critic (GAC), a zero-shot framework that combines frontier models' general-purpose reasoning with the planning competence of specialized driving models through an inference-time harness. In GAC, specialized planners generate multiple candidate trajectories and make an initial selection, while a frozen frontier model serves as an action critic that assesses the selected trajectory against scene evidence and either retains it or reselects from the available candidates. The harness combines camera images with spatial overlays, provides driving context and reasoning principles through textual instructions, and regulates the information available at each stage to support trajectory assessment and reselection. On HUGSIM, GAC raises DrivoR's HD-Score to 43.2, achieving state-of-the-art performance among methods trained without additional simulation data. GAC also consistently improves closed-loop driving safety across three planners, with relative HD-Score gains of up to 32.1%. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 further reveal how GAC improves planning performance by correcting up to 52.13% of eligible unsafe trajectory selections while introducing new failures in only 0.67% of originally high-quality selections. These results demonstrate the potential of harnessing frontier models to improve driving safety through inference-time cooperation with specialized planners.

潘佳老师实验室.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Xianzhe Fan, Chi-Pin Huang, Fu-En Yang, Jing Wang, Yecheng Wu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: MAWAM is a multi-agent model that enhances coordinated robotic manipulation by predicting joint actions and future states, achieving significant performance improvements in real and simulated tasks.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control: without attention, a four-arm relay falls from 95.0% to 39.0%, and without this supervision, Place Food falls from 78.0% to 47.0%.

潘佳老师实验室.title: OmniHarness: Harnessing Generalizable Visual Generation via Symbolic Policy Learning
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Xu Xu, Jinxiu Liu, Zhangbo Qiao, Cheng Song, Jiaxing Lu
潘佳老师实验室.summary: OmniHarness introduces a symbolic policy learning framework for autonomous visual generation, enhancing experience acquisition and knowledge reuse, achieving superior performance in diverse benchmarks.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Unified multimodal large language models and multi-agent systems have advanced visual generation. However, several limitations remain. (1) Experience acquisition is typically reactive, occurring only in response to downstream tasks. (2) Accumulated knowledge varies in relevance and reliability, making efficient and effective reuse challenging. To address these limitations, we introduce OmniHarness, a framework for generalizable visual generation via symbolic policy learning. Before downstream objectives are specified, self-directed inquiry autonomously generates and executes practice tasks, with selection guided by capability novelty and the current competence frontier. Verified workflows are abstracted into symbolic policies that encode experience for task families. Symbolic retrieval searches workflow metadata in stages rather than full parameterized workflows, using reliability tiers to prioritize reliable knowledge. Execution feedback updates these policies after each task, guiding subsequent retrieval and reuse while model parameters remain fixed. Experiments across six benchmarks demonstrate strong performance and generalizable visual generation capabilities. On ComfyBench's Creative tasks, OmniHarness achieves a 95.0% resolve rate, exceeding the strongest baseline by 27.5 percentage points.

潘佳老师实验室.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Zhaochen Guo, Yunke Wang, Siyu Xu, Zijian Wang, Chenghao Xia
潘佳老师实验室.summary: ReActWAM enhances world-action model efficiency by reducing redundant computations through action-intent-guided prefix skipping and prediction reuse, achieving significant speedups without compromising task success.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: World-action models (WAMs) often generate future visual states alongside robot actions, introducing substantial computational overhead during inference. During closed-loop execution, consecutive inference cycles often predict similar action sequences, leading to redundant computation. However, reducing this redundancy requires distinguishing consistent actions from changes that demand fresh computation. To address these challenges, we propose ReActWAM, a training-free framework that combines action-intent-guided prefix skipping with inner-chunk prediction reuse. A coarse-to-fine assessment evaluates motion changes, visual consistency, and action prediction conflicts. For eligible chunks, we draw on first-step differences to adapt the cached latent and network features to the current condition, providing an estimate at a later denoising step that bypasses the redundant prefix. Subsequent inference refines this estimate while reusing stable denoising predictions within the chunk. Experiments across LingBot-VA, FastWAM and the Cosmos family on LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrate $1.41\times$--$5.44\times$ GPU inference speedup, with minimal degradation in task success rates. Real-world experiments on a Franka Research 3 (FR3) robot further achieve $1.46\times$ end-to-end speedup while maintaining success rate.

潘佳老师实验室.title: ManipScope: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Instruction Following and Generalization in Robotic Manipulation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Jiacheng Li, Yaping Li, Congsheng Xu, Qingchen Liu, Haonan Wang
潘佳老师实验室.summary: ManipScope is a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating robotic instruction following and generalization in manipulation tasks, revealing significant discrepancies between task success and goal adherence.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Completing a manipulation task does not establish that a robot follows the requested goal rather than a familiar routine. ManipScope is an evaluation-only diagnostic benchmark for robotic instruction following under changed task requirements. Built on RoboTwin 2.0's simulation resources, it specifies 48 held-out scenes across six task families with explicit source-task links; policies are trained on unmodified RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrations, and no demonstrations of the scenes are provided, so success requires reusing skills under a changed request rather than fitting supplied examples. Beyond task success, ManipScope provides a chain of diagnostics in which each step tests one explanation of a failure. For twelve policy checkpoints, 84.6% of failures in 13,200 episodes on eleven selection scenes displace a distractor, and gripper records show that failed episodes usually grasp a non-target. When the target is reassigned among the candidates on identical initial states, ten checkpoints follow every instruction on 3.9% of 1,000 states, below the 16% of an instruction-blind chooser, while a GPT-6 agent run as positive control reaches 88%. The failure recurs on unmodified training tasks and is not explained by missing manipulation skills, so success in these scenes largely reflects instruction-independent preferences; two checkpoints trained on the same data nevertheless follow color instructions. In a feasibility test, letting an agent select the target and the policy execute partly restores instruction following. Case studies with future-video and internal-intervention probes further show that forecasts and execution can agree on the wrong target and that action changes need not transfer the goal. Success, consistency, and sensitivity must each be checked against the requested goal.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Can Reasoning and Image Description Enhance Yes/No Visual Mathematical Understanding?
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Guangcheng Song, Weichuan Wang, Linqi Song
潘佳老师实验室.summary: This paper demonstrates that explicit reasoning enhances Vision-Language Models' performance on visual mathematical questions, while textual descriptions may hinder comprehension.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general visual tasks, yet their ability to understand mathematical images remains limited. This paper investigates whether explicit reasoning and textual image descriptions can enhance VLMs' performance on binary yes/no visual mathematical questions. To achieve this, we curated a paired evaluation set to benchmark prominent open-source VLMs under varying prompt and input conditions. In particular, we leverage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and use textual descriptions, either replacing or augmenting visual inputs, to isolate and evaluate mathematical comprehension. Our results show that explicit reasoning improves performance, especially in paired consistency accuracy, while textual image descriptions do not consistently help and may degrade performance. These findings suggest that reasoning is important for stable visual mathematical judgement, whereas description-based intermediates require more careful design.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Trailblazer-F: Speculative Action-Flow Inference for Autonomous Driving
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Haibo Hu, Lianming Huang, Qiao Li, Nan Guan, Chun Jason Xue
潘佳老师实验室.summary: Trailblazer-F is a speculative action-flow inference framework that reduces inference latency in autonomous driving by enabling parallel evaluation of planned trajectories, achieving significant speedups while maintaining planning quality.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Driving world-action models generate planned trajectories through iterative action denoising, with each update depending on the preceding state. This sequential dependency incurs substantial inference latency, limiting timely planning. Speculative inference offers an opportunity to reduce this latency by predicting future denoising states for parallel target evaluation, but requires efficient proposal generation and suitable verification for continuous actions. We present Trailblazer-F, a speculative action-flow inference framework in which a lightweight drafter acts as a trailblazer, charting a candidate denoising path through the compact, structured waypoint space so that the target model can verify multiple steps in parallel and advance with fewer sequential updates. Our method maintains planning quality while keeping the pretrained target model frozen.Across all 12,146 NAVSIM v1 navtest scenes, Trailblazer-F maintains near-baseline planning performance, with PDMS changes of +0.04 and -0.08 points for SimWAM and DriveWAM, respectively. Paired inference measurements on an NVIDIA L20 GPU yield 2.31x and 1.55x speedups. Real-vehicle experiments on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin further demonstrate 1.96x and 1.37x speedups, together with close qualitative trajectory agreement with native sampling. our code is here https://github.com/DanileHaibo/Trailblazer-F

潘佳老师实验室.title: Perceive Once, Escalate on Demand: Handing Off Visual KV Memory from Small to Large VLMs
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Qiang Zhou, Jianing Deng, Siyan Dong, Jingxian Chen, Han-Yi Lin
潘佳老师实验室.summary: Baton enhances visual memory transfer from small to large VLMs, reducing computational costs while improving decision-making accuracy in embodied agents during video processing.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: An embodied agent cannot afford a large vision-language model (VLM) at every step of a long video, so a cascade runs a small VLM continuously and escalates only uncertain decisions to a large one. Each escalation, however, forces the large model to re-encode a history the small model has already perceived, and this dominates its cost. We present Baton, which hands the large model the small model's visual memory, its key-value (KV) cache over the history. Baton rests on one finding: the large model needs a usable memory, not a faithful copy of its own. A map trained to reproduce the large model's cache matches it most closely, yet brings no gain over the small model alone. Baton instead distills a per-layer linear map, without labels, from the large model's own answers, with the large model encoding only the current frame. Interventions on the map trace the gain to one direction, carried by the middle third of the large model's layers. On RoboMME, Baton beats the small model alone, a pruned or shortened re-watch, and a text memory; as the escalation channel of a cascade it matches re-watching to within about one point at 28-47% less compute, and 8x less per escalation at 64 frames. Its gain grows with the large model, from 8B to 32B, tracks the large model's headroom across eight model pairs from four families, and transfers zero-shot to OpenEQA.

潘佳老师实验室.title: Recursive Bayesian Monitoring of SLAM Failures for LiDAR-Based UAV Navigation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Mingqiao Han, Qigeng Duan, Xuchen Liu, Jinqiang Cui, Xi Chen
潘佳老师实验室.summary: This paper introduces a scene-geometry consistency monitor for detecting SLAM failures in LiDAR-based UAV navigation, enhancing safety without relying on prior maps or redundant sensing.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: SLAM failures remain difficult to avoid in autonomous robotic systems, and undetected failures can propagate to unsafe planning, control, and mission-level decisions. Existing monitoring strategies often depend on prior maps, estimator-internal variables, or redundant sensing, which limits their applicability to deployed and resource-constrained robots. This paper presents a scene-geometry consistency monitor for detecting geometry-manifested SLAM failures using only the geometric output of the SLAM backend. The targeted failures include cumulative drift-induced failures, abrupt misregistration failures, and backend map corruption when they become observable as inconsistency in reconstructed scene geometry. The proposed method represents revisited local regions with recursive latent voxel geometry and evaluates each current observation against a trusted continuation explanation and a weak non-propagated reference explanation. The resulting voxel-wise evidence contrasts are aggregated into a fixed-boundary monitoring signal for online failure declaration and downstream safety response. Experiments on self-collected sequences, GEODE benchmark sequences, multiple robotic platforms, and different SLAM backends show that the monitor responds to failures when they are manifested in backend scene geometry. It achieves 4/4 valid post-onset declarations with no pre-onset alarms on four self-collected sequences, detects geometry-manifested failures in all five corrupted GEODE runs while remaining alarm-free in five geometrically consistent runs, adds only 0.1--0.2\% absolute CPU load, and supports a closed-loop UAV detect--isolate--recover workflow.

潘佳老师实验室.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Rui Cao, Jia-Hui Pan, Yin Zhang, Qiwei Meng, Jiapeng Li
潘佳老师实验室.summary: UA-Depth is an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that improves robotic manipulation by refining depth and uncertainty for non-Lambertian objects, achieving superior performance across diverse benchmarks.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

潘佳老师实验室.title: See, Remember, Explore: A Benchmark and Baselines for Streaming Spatial Reasoning
潘佳老师实验室.authors_text: Yuxi Wei, Wei Huang, Qirui Chen, Lu Hou, Xiaojuan Qi
潘佳老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces S3-Bench, a benchmark for streaming spatial reasoning, and AMF-VLM, a model enhancing active exploration and memory efficiency, achieving significant performance improvements.
潘佳老师实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial understanding is fundamental for embodied agents, yet most spatial VLMs and benchmarks remain offline-evaluating post-hoc QA over pre-recorded inputs and overlooking two crucial deployment-critical requirements: long-horizon streaming inference and active perception when the current view is insufficient. To address this gap, we introduce S3-Bench, a benchmark suite for streaming spatial question answering with active exploration, where queries are temporally grounded to specific timestamps and must be answered using only observations available up to that moment. S3-Bench adopts a dual-domain design, combining a scalable simulator with controllable trajectories and exploration actions, and real-world streaming videos that capture practical sensing artifacts for rigorous generalization evaluation. Overall, it spans 10K+ scenes and 26K+ trajectories, with dedicated training (S3-Train) and evaluation (S3-Eval) splits. We further propose AMF-VLM, which supports streaming spatial reasoning under bounded computing via (i) memory folding, which compresses long-horizon observations into compact structured memory, and (ii) active exploration, which outputs explicit actions (e.g. move/rotate/scan) to acquire missing evidence before answering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, compared to models using identical training data, our approach yields improvements of 8.8% and 13.3% on the simulated and real splits of S3-Eval, respectively, while maintaining competitive transferability to standard spatial benchmarks.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Nie Lin, Takehiko Ohkawa, Sijin Chen, Ruoshi Wen, Zhuohang Li
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: SiMDex is a data mining framework that enhances robot dexterous manipulation by selectively curating relevant egocentric video samples, improving success rates significantly compared to random sampling.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Recent years have witnessed an explosive trend of scaling ego-centric human videos for robot manipulation, yet it remains unclear which data actually benefits dexterous manipulation. We present SiMDex, a similarity-based data mining framework that casts human data selection for VLA post-training in dexterous manipulation as a recommendation problem. For each robot demonstration, SiMDex runs a recall-ranking-re-ranking cascade over ~32M egocentric human samples: two stages, recall and ranking, select a task-relevant subset in a morphology-agnostic action space, and re-ranking verifies it on pixels, with no change to VLA architecture or training. Against a strong baseline trained with an equal amount of randomly sampled human data, SiMDex uses only ~1.49M mined samples (<5% of the pool) yet improves the overall success rate from 47.7% to 61.7%, showing that selective curation outperforms indiscriminate data mixing.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: AELF: Active Terrain-Aware UAV Exploration Using a Lightweight Framework
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Mingyang Li, Xiao Cao, Yi Luo, Yuting Tao, Hongjie Huang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The paper introduces AELF, a lightweight 2.5D mapping framework for efficient UAV exploration that adapts to terrain changes, enhancing performance in complex environments.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: This paper presents an efficient and robust approach for autonomous aerial exploration in complex environments. Instead of relying on conventional 3D voxel-based maps for exploration, we utilize a lightweight 2.5D map framework that reduces computational overhead while preserving essential topographic information. More importantly, this representation systematically eliminates the blind voxel problem commonly encountered in voxel-based exploration due to occlusions and limited visibility. Unlike previous methods that rely on a fixed altitude scale for exploration, our approach requires no prior height information and actively adapts to terrain elevation changes during exploration. To further enhance exploration efficiency while preserving the generality of 3D exploration, we perform 2D path planning on the 2.5D map framework, which is then lifted to 3D to evaluate the cost between viewpoints by taking into account terrain traversability, thereby reducing frequent altitude changes and enabling smoother exploration. Extensive experiments conducted in both simulated and real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of our approach over existing solutions. Our approach demonstrates fast exploration of over 2000~$\text{m}^2$ of cluttered forest and sloped mountainous terrain with elevation changes of up to 10~m, reaching a maximum speed of 5~m/s in real-world tests.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Xinxiang Yin, Xinglang Zhang, Haodong Chen, Zhiqing Cui, Weidong Tang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The paper presents Anchor, a self-evolving agent that optimizes memory retention through source decision testing, enhancing performance in long-horizon tasks by up to 19.9%.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The paper introduces Mega-MMDF, a comprehensive dataset for multimodal deepfake detection, and DeepfakeBench-MM, a standardized evaluation framework, enhancing detector performance across diverse forgery pipelines.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Zunhai Su, Keyu Fan, Ruishan Guo, Zhongzhu Zhou, Jingzehua Xu
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: QuantStream3D introduces a novel KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers, achieving significant accuracy and efficiency improvements through geometry-guided mixed-precision techniques.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch. Guided by these findings, we propose QuantStream3D, to our knowledge the first dedicated KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers. Compared with LLM-oriented KV quantizers, it reduces TUM absolute trajectory error and NeuralRGBD completeness error by up to 57.4% and 69.7%, respectively. Integration with existing native cache-pruning methods further pushes compression while improving reconstruction quality on NeuralRGBD. Our optimized StreamVGGT backend achieves $5.05\times$ physical KV compression and 23.1% lower latency at batch size one. Under a fixed memory budget on the same GPU, it supports $5.4\times$ the maximum batch size and up to $1.67\times$ the peak throughput of unquantized inference. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be made publicly available.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yun Yan, Shizhi Hu, Zhichao Li, Yang Guan, Shiqi Liu

A coarse-to-fine assessment evaluates motion changes, visual consistency, and action prediction conflicts. For eligible chunks, we draw on first-step differences to adapt the cached latent and network features to the current condition, providing an estimate at a later denoising step that bypasses the redundant prefix. Subsequent inference refines this estimate while reusing stable denoising predictions within the chunk. Experiments across LingBot-VA, FastWAM and the Cosmos family on LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrate $1.41\times$--$5.44\times$ GPU inference speedup, with minimal degradation in task success rates. Real-world experiments on a Franka Research 3 (FR3) robot further achieve $1.46\times$ end-to-end speedup while maintaining success rate.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: ManipScope: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Instruction Following and Generalization in Robotic Manipulation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Jiacheng Li, Yaping Li, Congsheng Xu, Qingchen Liu, Haonan Wang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: ManipScope is a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating robotic instruction following and generalization in manipulation tasks, revealing significant discrepancies between task success and goal adherence.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Completing a manipulation task does not establish that a robot follows the requested goal rather than a familiar routine. ManipScope is an evaluation-only diagnostic benchmark for robotic instruction following under changed task requirements. Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Can Reasoning and Image Description Enhance Yes/No Visual Mathematical Understanding?
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Guangcheng Song, Weichuan Wang, Linqi Song
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: This paper demonstrates that explicit reasoning enhances Vision-Language Models' performance on visual mathematical questions, while textual descriptions may hinder comprehension.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general visual tasks, yet their ability to understand mathematical images remains limited. This paper investigates whether explicit reasoning and textual image descriptions can enhance VLMs' performance on binary yes/no visual mathematical questions. To achieve this, we curated a paired evaluation set to benchmark prominent open-source VLMs under varying prompt and input conditions. In particular, we leverage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and use textual descriptions, either replacing or augmenting visual inputs, to isolate and evaluate mathematical comprehension. Our results show that explicit reasoning improves performance, especially in paired consistency accuracy, while textual image descriptions do not consistently help and may degrade performance. These findings suggest that reasoning is important for stable visual mathematical judgement, whereas description-based intermediates require more careful design.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Trailblazer-F: Speculative Action-Flow Inference for Autonomous Driving
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Haibo Hu, Lianming Huang, Qiao Li, Nan Guan, Chun Jason Xue
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Trailblazer-F is a speculative action-flow inference framework that reduces inference latency in autonomous driving by enabling parallel evaluation of planned trajectories, achieving significant speedups while maintaining planning quality.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Driving world-action models generate planned trajectories through iterative action denoising, with each update depending on the preceding state. This sequential dependency incurs substantial inference latency, limiting timely planning. Speculative inference offers an opportunity to reduce this latency by predicting future denoising states for parallel target evaluation, but requires efficient proposal generation and suitable verification for continuous actions. We present Trailblazer-F, a speculative action-flow inference framework in which a lightweight drafter acts as a trailblazer, charting a candidate denoising path through the compact, structured waypoint space so that the target model can verify multiple steps in parallel and advance with fewer sequential updates. Our method maintains planning quality while keeping the pretrained target model frozen.Across all 12,146 NAVSIM v1 navtest scenes, Trailblazer-F maintains near-baseline planning performance, with PDMS changes of +0.04 and -0.08 points for SimWAM and DriveWAM, respectively. Paired inference measurements on an NVIDIA L20 GPU yield 2.31x and 1.55x speedups. Real-vehicle experiments on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin further demonstrate 1.96x and 1.37x speedups, together with close qualitative trajectory agreement with native sampling. our code is here https://github.com/DanileHaibo/Trailblazer-F

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Perceive Once, Escalate on Demand: Handing Off Visual KV Memory from Small to Large VLMs
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Qiang Zhou, Jianing Deng, Siyan Dong, Jingxian Chen, Han-Yi Lin
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Baton enhances visual memory transfer from small to large VLMs, reducing computational costs while improving decision-making accuracy in embodied agents during video processing.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: An embodied agent cannot afford a large vision-language model (VLM) at every step of a long video, so a cascade runs a small VLM continuously and escalates only uncertain decisions to a large one. Each escalation, however, forces the large model to re-encode a history the small model has already perceived, and this dominates its cost. We present Baton, which hands the large model the small model's visual memory, its key-value (KV) cache over the history. Baton rests on one finding: the large model needs a usable memory, not a faithful copy of its own. A map trained to reproduce the large model's cache matches it most closely, yet brings no gain over the small model alone. Baton instead distills a per-layer linear map, without labels, from the large model's own answers, with the large model encoding only the current frame. Interventions on the map trace the gain to one direction, carried by the middle third of the large model's layers. On RoboMME, Baton beats the small model alone, a pruned or shortened re-watch, and a text memory; as the escalation channel of a cascade it matches re-watching to within about one point at 28-47% less compute, and 8x less per escalation at 64 frames. Its gain grows with the large model, from 8B to 32B, tracks the large model's headroom across eight model pairs from four families, and transfers zero-shot to OpenEQA.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Recursive Bayesian Monitoring of SLAM Failures for LiDAR-Based UAV Navigation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Mingqiao Han, Qigeng Duan, Xuchen Liu, Jinqiang Cui, Xi Chen
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: This paper introduces a scene-geometry consistency monitor for detecting SLAM failures in LiDAR-based UAV navigation, enhancing safety without relying on prior maps or redundant sensing.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: SLAM failures remain difficult to avoid in autonomous robotic systems, and undetected failures can propagate to unsafe planning, control, and mission-level decisions. Existing monitoring strategies often depend on prior maps, estimator-internal variables, or redundant sensing, which limits their applicability to deployed and resource-constrained robots. This paper presents a scene-geometry consistency monitor for detecting geometry-manifested SLAM failures using only the geometric output of the SLAM backend. The targeted failures include cumulative drift-induced failures, abrupt misregistration failures, and backend map corruption when they become observable as inconsistency in reconstructed scene geometry. The proposed method represents revisited local regions with recursive latent voxel geometry and evaluates each current observation against a trusted continuation explanation and a weak non-propagated reference explanation. The resulting voxel-wise evidence contrasts are aggregated into a fixed-boundary monitoring signal for online failure declaration and downstream safety response. Experiments on self-collected sequences, GEODE benchmark sequences, multiple robotic platforms, and different SLAM backends show that the monitor responds to failures when they are manifested in backend scene geometry. It achieves 4/4 valid post-onset declarations with no pre-onset alarms on four self-collected sequences, detects geometry-manifested failures in all five corrupted GEODE runs while remaining alarm-free in five geometrically consistent runs, adds only 0.1--0.2\% absolute CPU load, and supports a closed-loop UAV detect--isolate--recover workflow.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: UA-Depth: Uncertainty-Aware Depth Restoration for Material-Agnostic Object Manipulation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Rui Cao, Jia-Hui Pan, Yin Zhang, Qiwei Meng, Jiapeng Li
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: UA-Depth is an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that improves robotic manipulation by refining depth and uncertainty for non-Lambertian objects, achieving superior performance across diverse benchmarks.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation requires accurate metric depth, yet commodity RGB-D cameras often fail on non-Lambertian objects such as transparent, reflective, and translucent materials, producing holes, structured noise, and biased depth. Most restoration methods produce only a single depth map, treating noisy and reliable regions uniformly for downstream tasks while ignoring regional uncertainty. We present UA-Depth, an uncertainty-aware depth restoration framework that iteratively co-refines depth and pixel-wise uncertainty, and uses uncertainty-gated features to suppress unreliable cues for stable updates. To strengthen zero-shot behavior, UA-Depth leverages a frozen depth foundation model as a prior to initialize missing or unreliable depth, and applies two-stage MAD-weighted log-depth scale normalization to reduce outlier bias in relative-to-metric alignment. We introduce an eight-dataset zero-shot benchmark across diverse scenes, materials, and sensors. Across these benchmarks, UA-Depth achieves the best mean rank among representative baselines, with particularly strong gains on datasets dominated by transparent and reflective objects. Beyond depth metrics, we demonstrate downstream improvements in category-level 6D pose estimation and 6D grasp synthesis by exploiting the predicted uncertainty. \emph{Code, models, and data for training and evaluation will be released upon publication.}

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: See, Remember, Explore: A Benchmark and Baselines for Streaming Spatial Reasoning
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yuxi Wei, Wei Huang, Qirui Chen, Lu Hou, Xiaojuan Qi
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The paper introduces S3-Bench, a benchmark for streaming spatial reasoning, and AMF-VLM, a model enhancing active exploration and memory efficiency, achieving significant performance improvements.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Spatial understanding is fundamental for embodied agents, yet most spatial VLMs and benchmarks remain offline-evaluating post-hoc QA over pre-recorded inputs and overlooking two crucial deployment-critical requirements: long-horizon streaming inference and active perception when the current view is insufficient. To address this gap, we introduce S3-Bench, a benchmark suite for streaming spatial question answering with active exploration, where queries are temporally grounded to specific timestamps and must be answered using only observations available up to that moment. S3-Bench adopts a dual-domain design, combining a scalable simulator with controllable trajectories and exploration actions, and real-world streaming videos that capture practical sensing artifacts for rigorous generalization evaluation. Overall, it spans 10K+ scenes and 26K+ trajectories, with dedicated training (S3-Train) and evaluation (S3-Eval) splits. We further propose AMF-VLM, which supports streaming spatial reasoning under bounded computing via (i) memory folding, which compresses long-horizon observations into compact structured memory, and (ii) active exploration, which outputs explicit actions (e.g. move/rotate/scan) to acquire missing evidence before answering. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, compared to models using identical training data, our approach yields improvements of 8.8% and 13.3% on the simulated and real splits of S3-Eval, respectively, while maintaining competitive transferability to standard spatial benchmarks.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Junying Wang, Yijin Guo, Yalun Wu, Ziheng Jiao, Farong Wen
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: The paper introduces RoSci, a framework and benchmark for assessing and enhancing the robustness of Vision-Language Models in handling erroneous or incomplete scientific information.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable significant progress in scientific tasks. However, these models are generally assumed to be presented with complete and accurate information, overlooking the challenges of erroneous/missing information in wild scenarios. To address this gap, we introduce the concept of Scientific Model Robustness, which defines a model's ability to detect anomalies, assess solvability, and perform self-calibration when faced with Information Error (inconsistencies) or Information Loss (insufficiency). Specifically, we present RoSci-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,220 samples using a seed-variant strategy across six degradation types. To address VLM fragility, we further propose RoSci-Agent, a framework that employs a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline to vet premises before reasoning. The evaluated VLMs sometimes answer questions whose premises are invalid or incomplete. RoSci-Agent achieves a higher Overall Robustness Score than the evaluated standalone VLMs. RoSci-Bench gives the multimodal reasoning community a common test of when models answer, request clarification, or reject a scientific question.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Nie Lin, Takehiko Ohkawa, Sijin Chen, Ruoshi Wen, Zhuohang Li
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: SiMDex is a data mining framework that enhances robot dexterous manipulation by selectively curating relevant egocentric video samples, improving success rates significantly compared to random sampling.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Recent years have witnessed an explosive trend of scaling ego-centric human videos for robot manipulation, yet it remains unclear which data actually benefits dexterous manipulation. We present SiMDex, a similarity-based data mining framework that casts human data selection for VLA post-training in dexterous manipulation as a recommendation problem. For each robot demonstration, SiMDex runs a recall-ranking-re-ranking cascade over ~32M egocentric human samples: two stages, recall and ranking, select a task-relevant subset in a morphology-agnostic action space, and re-ranking verifies it on pixels, with no change to VLA architecture or training. Against a strong baseline trained with an equal amount of randomly sampled human data, SiMDex uses only ~1.49M mined samples (<5% of the pool) yet improves the overall success rate from 47.7% to 61.7%, showing that selective curation outperforms indiscriminate data mixing.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: SOAR: Training-Free Rank-Consistent Rollout Compression for Latent World Model Planning
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Anqi Li, Kai Liu, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: SOAR is a training-free method that optimizes rollout compression in latent world model planning, achieving significant speedups while maintaining ranking accuracy across various tasks.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Latent world models plan by rolling out hundreds of candidate action sequences through a transformer predictor, so a single decision can take tens of seconds. Existing accelerations prune spatial tokens as in vision-language models, yet a sampling-based planner uses predicted costs only to rank candidates, so a rollout can be compressed freely as long as the ranking survives. We propose SOAR, a training-free method that adapts rollout compression to each planning decision. At every decision, SOAR probes a few candidates under several token budgets and keeps the smallest budget that preserves their ranking, so it compresses as far as the current decision allows, without task labels. A closed-loop study of more than 80,000 episodes fixes the rest of the rollout: the first step, which alone reads a real observation, stays exact, and the context frame is cached rather than recomputed. On seven navigation and manipulation tasks with frozen checkpoints, SOAR matches dense-level planning success at 2.3x speedup and retains 98% at 2.5x. Our code is available at https://github.com/starrywiki/SOAR.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: $γ$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Xiaotao Zhang, Lin Qian, Hao Zhang, Xuanrui Cui, Yuehao Huang
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: $γ$-Scape is a simulation platform enabling mobile embodied agents to learn and adapt behaviors through interaction, tool use, and structured task objectives in a persistent environment.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Recent embodied agents construct and adapt robot behavior through executable programs, tool use, and interaction feedback. Studying these systems in mobile manipulation calls for physical worlds that connect agent-directed execution with its physical consequences and reusable interaction experience. We introduce $γ$-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform for mobile embodied intelligence. Agents compose motion tools and learned skills to carry out complete tasks that combine navigation and manipulation in a persistent physical world. BenchForge grounds structured objectives in physical task instances with instructions, reference programs, and goal evaluators, defining task goals while preserving agents' choice of valid solutions. An agentic collection harness further enables agents to produce demonstrations by carrying out contact-rich interactions through sustained control and physical feedback. Assisted reference execution and human guidance provide complementary experience. The resulting tool traces and aligned observation-action records support program refinement and policy learning, with common task-goal criteria for subsequent evaluation. We benchmark representative agent systems on complete tasks and demonstrate contact collection and trace-informed program revision. Together, these workflows provide infrastructure for research on embodied recursive self-improvement.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: ManipScope: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Instruction Following and Generalization in Robotic Manipulation
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Jiacheng Li, Yaping Li, Congsheng Xu, Qingchen Liu, Haonan Wang

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: S2D-Splat: Static-First Gaussian Reconstruction of Dynamic Driving Scenes with Layer-Wise Feature Guidance
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Jinheng Li, Tianchen Deng, Bufan Zhang, Qu Chen, Jianwu Fang
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: S2D-Splat introduces a static-first Gaussian reconstruction framework that effectively separates static and dynamic features, enhancing camera estimation and geometry recovery in dynamic driving scenes.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Moving objects introduce cross-frame inconsistencies that complicate camera estimation and static geometry recovery in driving scenes. Recent feed-forward Gaussian methods explicitly separate static and dynamic primitives, but often estimate camera parameters and geometry from shared features that jointly encode both components, leaving static reconstruction susceptible to dynamic interference. To address this challenge, we propose S2D-Splat, a feed-forward framework for static-first Gaussian reconstruction with layer-wise feature guidance. Our framework separates static and dynamic features before camera and geometry estimation, enabling the static branch to recover camera parameters and static 3D Gaussians with reduced dynamic interference. Intermediate static features are cached at each layer and reused as fixed conditioning at corresponding layers of the dynamic branch. This asymmetric information flow preserves the established static representations while providing stable geometric context for reconstructing dynamic 3D Gaussians. An instance-level motion decoder further queries the fused static and dynamic representations to estimate object trajectories, supporting motion-aligned Gaussian fusion and temporal interpolation. Experiments on Waymo and zero-shot evaluations on nuScenes and the MM-AU accident dataset demonstrate that S2D-Splat outperforms existing approaches on most evaluated metrics and generalizes to highly dynamic, pre-collision driving scenarios.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: Moment-Video: Diagnosing Temporal Fidelity of Video MLLMs on Momentary Visual Events
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.authors_text: Xiaolin Liu, Yilun Zhu, Xiangyu Zhao, Xuehui Wang, Yan Li
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.summary: Moment-Video introduces a benchmark to evaluate video MLLMs' ability to identify and utilize brief, critical visual events, revealing significant performance gaps and localization challenges.
数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.debug_abstract: Video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in general and long-form video understanding, yet their ability to capture and use brief, answer-critical visual evidence remains underexplored. Momentary actions or state transitions may determine an answer while occupying only a small fraction of the video. Performance on broad video understanding tasks alone does not establish whether models can reliably identify and use this temporally localized evidence. We introduce Moment-Video, a benchmark for evaluating temporal fidelity through momentary visual event understanding. Questions are constructed around visually observable events or event sequences, requiring models to notice, count, describe, or reason about transient evidence. The benchmark contains 1,000 human-verified video-QA pairs across seven domains and 25 subcategories, covering four tasks: Temporal Occurrence, Temporal Counting, Action Description, and Temporal Reasoning. We evaluate 34 proprietary and open-source MLLMs. Under the main evaluation settings, the best-performing model, Seed-2.0-Pro, achieves 39.6% overall accuracy, while most open-source models remain below 25%. Diagnostic analyses show that denser frame sampling improves some models, but substantial errors persist in an audited subset even when human review judges the sampled visual evidence sufficient to answer. Performance also declines on longer videos, suggesting additional temporal-localization challenges. By exposing these limitations, Moment-Video provides a diagnostic benchmark to guide the evaluation and development of video MLLMs that more reliably understand brief, answer-critical visual events.

数字媒体与计算机视觉实验室.title: See, Remember, Explore: A Benchmark and Baselines for Streaming Spatial Reasoning

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Shengze Huang, Yanyu Mao, Xiaofei Yu, Baoshen Guo, Xiaorui Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: HookEvo is a framework that enhances tool-using agents by coordinating plugin evolution through lifecycle hooks, achieving significant performance improvements across various benchmarks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, the selected harnesses lead the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons, achieving 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench. Across three improvers and three edit scopes, from skill text to single-component and coordinated executable edits, GPT-6.1 Sol shows the largest average gain from the broadest scope. Our code is available at https://huangshengzebluesky.github.io/hookevo/.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Xinxiang Yin, Xinglang Zhang, Haodong Chen, Zhiqing Cui, Weidong Tang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper presents Anchor, a self-evolving agent that optimizes memory retention through source decision testing, enhancing performance in long-horizon tasks by up to 19.9%.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: StreamPro: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Grained Rewards for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Ao Li, Zihan Xiao, Zihao Yue, Boshen Xu, Linli Yao
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: StreamPro introduces a two-stage reinforcement learning framework with multi-grained rewards to enhance proactive streaming video understanding, significantly outperforming existing benchmarks.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to continuously monitor evolving video streams and decide whether, when, and what to respond. However, training models with such proactive capabilities remains challenging. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) suffers from severe imbalance between silence and response signals, while reinforcement learning (RL) faces sparse response-level rewards and difficulties in optimizing interdependent response sequences. To address these challenges, we propose StreamPro, a two-stage training framework. We first introduce CB-Stream Loss to alleviate supervision imbalance during SFT. 情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents Anchor, a self-evolving agent that optimizes memory retention through source decision testing, enhancing performance in long-horizon tasks by up to 19.9%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ao Li, Zihan Xiao, Zihao Yue, Boshen Xu, Linli Yao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: StreamPro introduces a two-stage reinforcement learning framework with multi-grained rewards to enhance proactive streaming video understanding, significantly outperforming existing benchmarks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to continuously monitor evolving video streams and decide whether, when, and what to respond. However, training models with such proactive capabilities remains challenging. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) suffers from severe imbalance between silence and response signals, while reinforcement learning (RL) faces sparse response-level rewards and difficulties in optimizing interdependent response sequences. To address these challenges, we propose StreamPro, a two-stage training framework. We first introduce CB-Stream Loss to alleviate supervision imbalance during SFT. We then employ Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with two complementary rewards: a refined Response-Matching (RM) reward that provides denser feedback for individual response decisions, and a rubric-based Sequence-Quality (SQ) reward that encourages globally coherent response sequences. To support the two training stages, we construct StreamPro-SFT-63K and StreamPro-RL-3K, respectively. To address the limited task coverage of existing proactive benchmarks, we further introduce StreamPro-Bench, encompassing three task categories: Perceptual Understanding, Temporal Reasoning, and Anticipatory Assistance, along with StreamPro-F1 to evaluate response correctness, timing, and frequency. Experiments demonstrate that StreamPro substantially improves proactive streaming video understanding, achieving an average StreamPro-F1 of 32.8 on StreamPro-Bench, compared with 9.2 for the strongest baseline, while maintaining strong performance on real-time streaming tasks, reaching 79.8 on StreamingBench-RTVU.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: LoopNav: Benchmarking Spatial Consistency in World Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Kewei Lian, Shaofei Cai, Yitao Liang, Anji Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: LoopNav introduces a benchmark and dataset for evaluating spatial consistency in world models through loop-based navigation in Minecraft, addressing gaps in existing datasets.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: The ability to simulate the world in a spatially consistent manner is a crucial requirement for effective world models. Such a model enables high-quality visual generation, and also ensures the reliability of world models for downstream tasks such as simulation and planning. It must not only retain long-horizon observational information, but also enables the construction of explicit or implicit internal spatial representations. However, existing datasets do not explicitly enforce spatial consistency constraints, limiting both the ability to systematically evaluate this capability and to learn it through data-driven approaches. Furthermore, most existing benchmarks primarily emphasize visual coherence or generation quality, neglecting the requirement of long-range spatial consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose LoopNav, a dataset and corresponding benchmark centered on loop-based navigation for evaluating spatial consistency. The dataset comprises 200 hours of loop-based navigation videos with actions, collected from diverse locations in the open-world environment of Minecraft. We further introduce a Scene Graph Consistency Score(SGCS) to quantify spatial consistency while remaining invariant to pixel-level variations. Dataset, benchmark, and code are open-sourced to support future research.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper explores LLM agent behavior through statistical physics, introducing agent states and a partition function to model post-training transitions and potential structures.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: There has been significant recent interest in understanding the behaviour of LLM agents from the perspective of human preferences or corpus statistics. In this paper we propose agent states as intermediate variables through which post-training can be measured and predicted. From a statistical physics perspective, we study the emergence of a global potential which governs the transition of state in LLM agent reasoning. We introduce a partition function to model the ideal KL-regularised transition distribution and track potential structure, mean reward and state entropy. We demonstrate our approach in two Qwen3.5-9B tasks: safety-test selection and physics-reasoning auditing. We observe that the potential structure strengthens during post-training as predicted from our framework, while joint changes in reward and state entropy provide consistency evidence. States thus provide a quantitative description of how post-training organises agent behaviour.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Beyond a Single Human Demonstration: Learning from Scored Trajectory Alternatives for End-to-End Driving
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xinyao Rao, Zecheng Tang, Liuxuan Sun, Zheyuan Lai, Minjun Yu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: DriveSTA enhances end-to-end driving by generating diverse trajectory alternatives for improved supervision and efficiency, achieving state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing inference latency.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Human driving logs record only one trajectory per scene, leaving other feasible driving choices without explicit trajectory targets or quality labels. This limits supervision for end-to-end planners that generate and refine multiple candidate trajectories. Meanwhile, conditioning refinement on a large vision-language model adds substantial online inference cost. We propose DriveSTA, which extends autoregressive proposal generation and proposal-conditioned residual flow refinement with scored trajectory alternatives. For each training scene, we generate alternatives offline through smooth deformations of the recorded trajectory and evaluate their simulated execution against logged traffic. Diverse, high-quality alternatives supervise distinct proposals and define residual targets for quality-guided denoising, while candidates spanning the full score range train a scorer to assess driving quality. A shared joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), adapted through masked video-feature prediction, encodes observed frames once and provides temporal context for both refinement and scoring. On NAVSIM v1 Navtest, DriveSTA ranks first among the compared planners trained on NAVSIM data alone. With expanded training data, DriveSTA-Scale achieves state-of-the-art results among the compared methods on Navtest and closed-loop HUGSIM, while reducing mean planner forward-pass latency by 73% relative to ChainFlow-VLA in matched evaluations.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: AceVLN: Asynchronous Cloud Edge Deployment of VLNs via Latent Scheduling and Compensation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zihao Zheng, Hangyu Cao, Yulong Han, Xichang Wu, Zhihao Mao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: AceVLN is a training-free framework that enhances asynchronous dual-system VLN on robots by improving navigation accuracy and efficiency through active latent refresh and edge-side compensation.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Cloud--edge deployment enables asynchronous dual-system VLN on resource-constrained robots, but inference and communication delays cause latent mismatch and navigation errors. Existing adaptation methods reuse historical guidance but cannot provide updated navigation information when it becomes inadequate. We propose AceVLN, a training-free framework for active latent refresh and edge-side compensation. Our analysis reveals that action-relevant mismatch is concentrated in a compact Critical Subspace and can be tracked through fast-system feature drift. Critical Feature Drift Entropy reflects navigation sensitivity and guides adaptive refresh, while Critical Drift Continuity indicates when recent latent updates can support compensation during latency spikes. AceVLN integrates subspace-decoupled mismatch modeling, entropy-guided refresh scheduling, and continuity-guided compensation. Experiments show that \textit{AceVLN} improves success rates by 1.7--2.4 percentage points over the strongest baselines, while reducing amortized computation time by 2.7--10.0\% and FLOPs by 18.4--22.3\%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: SCAP: Stochastic Context for Action Expert Pretraining
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xiao Lin, Yaoxu Lyu, Ronghao Dang, Zhili Liu, Kaijing Ma
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: SCAP enhances vision-language-action pretraining by masking inputs to preserve joint modeling pathways, improving performance and reducing reliance on visual shortcuts in robotic tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Single-modality action-expert pretraining controls competition from visual shortcuts before vision--language--action (VLA) adaptation. Yet single-modality pretraining can impair the vision--language interactions needed for subsequent joint prediction. We construct a diagnostic model in which VA or LA pretraining can disable an initially active pathway for joint vision--language modeling. In this model, subsequent training with complete visual and language inputs cannot restore the pathway, even with unlimited adaptation. We therefore introduce Stochastic Context for Action Expert Pretraining (SCAP), a new action-expert pretraining stage that precedes full-input training. During this stage, visual and text tokens are randomly masked before entering the VLM. In this unified diagnostic model, SCAP can preserve the joint vision--language modeling pathway during pretraining and subsequent full-input training. Compared with direct full-input training, it can also reduce reliance on visual shortcuts and increase reliance on language instructions. SCAP consistently improves performance across four different VLA architectures. In real-robot experiments, it achieves 76.67% average success across three instruction-conditioned manipulation tasks, outperforming full-input pretraining by 25 percentage points.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Guangyu Zhao, Yongchang Zhang, Ruizhang Jiang, Zhihong Yu, Yuhao Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MomentMem introduces a hierarchical architecture for robotic manipulation that effectively retains key visual moments, achieving significant performance improvements in long-horizon tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. Existing approaches typically rely on full observation histories, which become redundant over long horizons, or text summaries, which may omit precise visual details. We study visual moment memory, the ability to retain such details from key moments for subsequent manipulation. To support this study, we introduce VMBench, a suite of long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring memory of spatial locations, visual appearances, and their associations. We further propose MomentMem, a hierarchical architecture in which a VLM-based memorizer selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions conditioned on the selected memories. This separation enables us to evaluate memory selection alongside closed-loop task success and to study memorizer generalization independently of the executor. On VMBench, MomentMem achieves 49.9% average success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 31.7 percentage points. Moreover, we find that the memorizer transfers well to unseen appearances zero-shot. It can also adapt to an unseen task with only a few memory annotations, reaching 43.7% success, close to the 44.3% obtained with full memory supervision. Further experiments show competitive performance on RMBench and improvements in real-robot manipulation. These results highlight the value of retaining sparse visual evidence for memory-dependent manipulation. Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/MomentMem.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: 2D or 3D? Rethinking Token Pruning in 3D VLAs with Cross-Modal Correlation Awareness
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zihao Zheng, Zhihao Mao, Quanyou Li, Hangyu Cao, Sicheng Tian
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The 2Dor3D framework optimizes token pruning in 3D vision-language-action models by leveraging cross-modal correlations, achieving significant inference speedups with minimal impact on task success rates.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: 3D vision-language-action (VLA) models process both image and point cloud tokens at each control step, increasing the cost of action prediction. Token pruning can reduce this cost, but a token's contribution depends on which other tokens remain. We present 2Dor3D, a framework that jointly selects which 2D and 3D tokens to retain under a fixed token budget. Our analysis shows that either modality can compensate for the other within a patch, that neighboring correlations help explain differences in pruning risk, and that shared tokens couple pruning decisions across patches. In one box-closing observation, two patches with nearly identical interaction scores differed eightfold in the action deviation caused by removing their image token. Guided by these findings, 2Dor3D transfers cross-modal prediction residuals to retained tokens, uses neighborhood correlation entropy to explore more retention choices at local outliers, and updates pruning costs after each proposed exchange between coupled regions. A fused GPU kernel packs the selected tokens into a shorter sequence for subsequent Transformer layers. Across RLBench and LIBERO, 2Dor3D speeds up end-to-end inference by $2.06$--$2.10\times$ on MLA and $1.86$--$1.91\times$ on FiS-VLA, with task success rates 0.5--0.6 percentage points below the corresponding unpruned models.

HMI Lab.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
HMI Lab.authors_text: Shengze Huang, Yanyu Mao, Xiaofei Yu, Baoshen Guo, Xiaorui Wang
HMI Lab.summary: HookEvo is a framework that enhances tool-using agents by coordinating plugin evolution through lifecycle hooks, achieving significant performance improvements across various benchmarks.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, the selected harnesses lead the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons, achieving 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench. Across three improvers and three edit scopes, from skill text to single-component and coordinated executable edits, GPT-6.1 Sol shows the largest average gain from the broadest scope. Our code is available at https://huangshengzebluesky.github.io/hookevo/.
