上海人工智能实验室.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Junying Wang, Yijin Guo, Yalun Wu, Ziheng Jiao, Farong Wen
上海人工智能实验室.summary: The paper introduces RoSci, a framework and benchmark for assessing and enhancing the robustness of Vision-Language Models in handling erroneous or incomplete scientific information.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable significant progress in scientific tasks. However, these models are generally assumed to be presented with complete and accurate information, overlooking the challenges of erroneous/missing information in wild scenarios. To address this gap, we introduce the concept of Scientific Model Robustness, which defines a model's ability to detect anomalies, assess solvability, and perform self-calibration when faced with Information Error (inconsistencies) or Information Loss (insufficiency). Specifically, we present RoSci-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,220 samples using a seed-variant strategy across six degradation types. To address VLM fragility, we further propose RoSci-Agent, a framework that employs a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline to vet premises before reasoning. The evaluated VLMs sometimes answer questions whose premises are invalid or incomplete. RoSci-Agent achieves a higher Overall Robustness Score than the evaluated standalone VLMs. RoSci-Bench gives the multimodal reasoning community a common test of when models answer, request clarification, or reject a scientific question.

上海人工智能实验室.title: TrajRealm: A Large-Scale Point Tracking Dataset with Diverse Dynamics
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Ni Yang, Weiguang Zhao, Jiafei Cao, Yankai Jiang, Haoyu Guo
上海人工智能实验室.summary: TrajRealm is a large-scale synthetic point tracking dataset with ten million frames, offering diverse dynamics and precise annotations to enhance tracking method performance.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: General-purpose point tracking requires large-scale training data with diverse dynamics, yet existing datasets struggle to combine rich dynamic content, accurate scene geometry, and sufficient scale. We introduce TrajRealm, the first public synthetic point-tracking dataset to reach the ten-million-frame scale, constructed from games and embodied simulations. TrajRealm uses the rich environments and motion systems of modern games to capture diverse targets, activities, and interactions across diverse worlds, while embodied simulations add robot manipulation and indoor navigation data. The dataset provides RGB observations, depth, camera parameters, and persistent 2D and 3D point trajectories. These annotations provide precise, geometrically consistent supervision across foreground objects and static environmental surfaces. We also build TrajRealm-Bench with eight subcategories under Interaction and Locomotion to evaluate tracking across diverse scenes. Benchmark evaluations reveal the strengths and limitations of existing trackers in handling complex motion and maintaining long-term point correspondences. Training on TrajRealm improves the performance of existing tracking methods on synthetic and real-world benchmarks.

南开大学.title: HermiteTwin: Bicubic Hermite Shell Digital Twins for Contact-Rich Deformable Manipulation
南开大学.authors_text: Kangrui Zhang, Mu Huang, Xing Shen, Tiantian Liu, Bo Ren
南开大学.summary: HermiteTwin introduces a framework for reconstructing and simulating thin deformable objects by separately modeling deformation and contact, significantly improving manipulation accuracy over existing methods.
南开大学.debug_abstract: While existing methods for reconstructing deformable object manipulation have made impressive progress, they typically represent a thin object with a single particle set that must serve two purposes at once: modeling bending, and resolving contact with the robot. To bridge this gap, we present HermiteTwin, a framework that reconstructs a physical digital twin of a thin deformable object from multiview video of a robot manipulating it. Our key idea is to represent deformation and contact separately, each at its own resolution. The object is simulated as a bicubic Hermite shell, a coarse grid of $C^1$ elements whose nodal positions and derivatives define a smooth surface with Kirchhoff--Love bending, while the gripper acts through dense samples in material space that are captured, clamped, and released, and whose attachment forces reach the shell through the Hermite basis. This decoupling keeps the physical state compact while contact stays fine-grained. We identify effective material and contact parameters with CMA-ES followed by adjoint-based refinement, and drive a reconstructed Gaussian appearance model with the simulated shell. In experiments on real cloth and foam manipulation, HermiteTwin outperforms the state-of-the-art spring--mass twin across reconstruction, resimulation, and future prediction.

四川大学.title: Embodied Interaction Policy: A Unified Model for Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction
四川大学.authors_text: Youqiang Gui, Yunfei Liu, Lijian Lin, Ye Zhu, Jianan Wang
四川大学.summary: The Embodied Interaction Policy (EIP) integrates speech and motion generation for enhanced real-time human-robot interaction, improving coordination, motion quality, and user experience.
四川大学.debug_abstract: Real-time human-robot social interaction requires continuous coordination between speech and physical behavior. Existing systems often separate interaction agents from motion generation, complicating coordination as conversational states change. We propose \textbf{Embodied Interaction Policy (EIP)}, a unified streaming framework that couples an Audio-Interaction expert with a motion expert through layer-wise joint attention. This allows motion generation to directly access the evolving interaction context. A chunk-wise causal mask prevents access to future context, while a vocal token encodes speaking state and the semantic emotion of the response. We construct \textbf{Embodied Interaction Dataset (EI-Data)} from co-speech and dyadic interaction data and train our model in two stages to learn state-adaptive and emotion-conditioned behavior. Combined with the frozen interaction expert, EIP supports continuous robot motion during proactive responses and interruption-aware turn-taking. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate improved motion quality over representative gesture-generation baselines. Compared with a representative cascaded system, EIP achieves higher interaction success and reduces warm-start latency by 64\%. Physical deployment and user studies further demonstrate improved motion naturalness and interaction comfort.

深圳大学.title: GeoSDF-Diff: Geometry-Aware Diffusion Planning for Collision-Free Trajectories
深圳大学.authors_text: Yueming Li, Zhanjiang Yang, Yang Shen, Meng Li, Lijun Sun
深圳大学.summary: GeoSDF-Diff enhances diffusion-based motion planning by integrating multi-scale SDF features for improved geometric feasibility in complex environments, achieving a 65.2% success rate.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Diffusion models have recently attracted increasing attention in motion planning due to their ability to model high-dimensional and multi-modal trajectory distributions. However, existing diffusion-based planners still struggle to reliably satisfy geometric feasibility in unseen cluttered environments with complex obstacle layouts. To address this challenge, we propose GeoSDF-Diff, a geometry-aware diffusion planner that incorporates multi-scale SDF conditioning into trajectory denoising. The key idea is to provide the denoiser with both route-level geometric context and fine local clearance evidence, enabling generated trajectories to better adapt to unseen complex obstacle layouts. Specifically, a Geometric Encoder extracts multi-scale SDF features and injects them into a DiT-X denoiser through cross-attention. We further introduce a trajectory-level training objective that combines SDF clearance, violation emphasis, smoothness, and path-length regularization, so that local infeasibilities are penalized during training rather than corrected only at inference time. Experiments on held-out cluttered environments show that, without post-hoc trajectory repair or sampling-time guidance, GeoSDF-Diff achieves a 65.2% average success rate across diverse test scenarios, outperforming strong diffusion baselines by 25.4% to 28.5%.

具身智能实验室.title: PanoUAV-Track: Full-Spherical UAV Visual Tracking in the Wild
具身智能实验室.authors_text: Bingyu Li, Lichang Yang, Zhiyuan Zhao, Junyu Gao, Xuelong Li
具身智能实验室.summary: The paper introduces PanoUAV-Track, a benchmark for UAV visual tracking using omnidirectional cameras, addressing geometric challenges and proposing the PUTrack framework for improved tracking performance.
具身智能实验室.debug_abstract: Existing UAV tracking benchmarks predominantly rely on perspective cameras with limited fields of view. Omnidirectional cameras enable full-spherical observation, yet tracking from moving UAV platforms remains largely unexplored. Unlike ground-level panoramic tracking, UAV-mounted omnidirectional cameras observe targets across both azimuth and elevation, introducing geometric challenges under equirectangular projection (ERP). To investigate this setting, we capture approximately \textbf{40 hours of real-world 8K panoramic UAV video} and construct \textbf{PanoUAV-Track} through temporal clip extraction, target annotation, and the integration of simulated sequences. The resulting benchmark comprises 1,895 sequences, 507,961 frames, and 2,872 annotated objects, covering real-world daytime and nighttime scenes alongside simulation, and supporting both visual and language-based target specification. Through extensive evaluations, we reveal a clear \textbf{perspective-to-spherical} generalization gap and identify tracking degradation associated with latitude-dependent distortion and ERP seam discontinuity. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{PanoUAV-Tracker (PUTrack)}, a geometry-aware tracking framework combining latitude-adaptive search and seam-aware periodic sampling. PUTrack improves zero-shot and in-domain tracking, particularly for seam-crossing targets. Code and benchmark resources will be available\footnote{\textcolor{tabpink}{https://libingyu01.github.io/PanoUAV-Track/}}.

中国人民大学.title: NavRSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Vision-and-Language Navigation
中国人民大学.authors_text: Guangzhao Dai, Guoxin Lian, Shuo Wang, Shengbin Yue, Qianru Sun
中国人民大学.summary: NavRSI is a recursive self-improvement framework that enhances vision-and-language navigation by optimizing LLM interactions through iterative harness revisions and closed-loop experience.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have enabled vision-and-language navigation (VLN) through direct closed-loop perception and action. However, navigation performance depends strongly on the harness governing LLM-environment interactions, while existing harnesses largely rely on manually designed navigation tools, memory, and agent roles. We introduce NavRSI, a harness-centric recursive self-improvement framework that optimizes the navigation behavior of frozen LLMs through closed-loop experience. In each round, NavRSI iteratively collects navigation trajectories and failure diagnostics, employs a designer agent to rewrite the harness, and retains the revisions that prove effective, while the designer accumulates experience from previous revisions so that the harness and this experience co-evolve. Privileged simulator diagnostics guide only the designer and remain inaccessible to the navigating LLM, enabling deployment with a single RGB camera and primitive actions, without task-specific model training or additional navigation tools. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across LLMs from four vendors, with 85.64% success rate on the full R2R-CE val-unseen split with GPT-6-Astra, surpassing the previously reported best by 4.13%. Evaluations on RxR-CE, NavRAG-CE, and a real humanoid robot further demonstrate its generalizability.

中国人民大学.title: Beyond Future Views: Exploring Future-State World Models for Vision-Language Navigation
中国人民大学.authors_text: Kangyi Wu, Pengna Li, Yucheng Wang, Yance Fang, Xihan Ma
中国人民大学.summary: The paper introduces FS-Nav, a future-state world modeling framework for Vision-Language Navigation that enhances performance by predicting goal-directed spatial states and route structures.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Vision-Language Navigation(VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through unseen 3D environments, where the target spaces often lie beyond the current observation. Navigation world models address this challenge by predicting future views either as pixels or latent representations, providing valuable look-ahead information for action decision. Both paradigms define the future primarily through what the agent may observe, raising a fundamental question: is predicting future views the ultimate form to represent the future for VLN? Cognitive studies show that the human hippocampus prospectively represents both future goals and intervening locations along planned routes. Inspired by this predictive-map view, we organize the navigation-relevant future around goal-directed spatial states and route structure. We instantiate this perspective with two complementary abstractions: a short-horizon waypoint that specifies the next local state to reach, and a mid-horizon corridor that captures the spatial support of the upcoming route. Based on this design, we propose FS-Nav, a future-state world modeling framework that predicts waypoint-corridor states from spatial memory and language instructions, and communicates them to a VLM navigator through top-down and first-person interfaces. Experiments on standard VLN benchmarks demonstrate that FS-Nav achieves state-of-the-art performance. This highlights navigation-relevant future-state modeling as a promising direction for representing the future in VLN.

中国人民大学.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
中国人民大学.authors_text: Shengze Huang, Yanyu Mao, Xiaofei Yu, Baoshen Guo, Xiaorui Wang
中国人民大学.summary: HookEvo is a framework that enhances tool-using agents by coordinating plugin evolution through lifecycle hooks, achieving significant performance improvements across various benchmarks.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, the selected harnesses lead the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons, achieving 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench. Across three improvers and three edit scopes, from skill text to single-component and coordinated executable edits, GPT-6.1 Sol shows the largest average gain from the broadest scope. Our code is available at https://huangshengzebluesky.github.io/hookevo/.

中国人民大学.title: StreamPro: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Grained Rewards for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
中国人民大学.authors_text: Ao Li, Zihan Xiao, Zihao Yue, Boshen Xu, Linli Yao
中国人民大学.summary: StreamPro introduces a two-stage reinforcement learning framework with multi-grained rewards to enhance proactive streaming video understanding, significantly outperforming existing benchmarks.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to continuously monitor evolving video streams and decide whether, when, and what to respond. However, training models with such proactive capabilities remains challenging. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) suffers from severe imbalance between silence and response signals, while reinforcement learning (RL) faces sparse response-level rewards and difficulties in optimizing interdependent response sequences. To address these challenges, we propose StreamPro, a two-stage training framework. We first introduce CB-Stream Loss to alleviate supervision imbalance during SFT. We then employ Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with two complementary rewards: a refined Response-Matching (RM) reward that provides denser feedback for individual response decisions, and a rubric-based Sequence-Quality (SQ) reward that encourages globally coherent response sequences. To support the two training stages, we construct StreamPro-SFT-63K and StreamPro-RL-3K, respectively. To address the limited task coverage of existing proactive benchmarks, we further introduce StreamPro-Bench, encompassing three task categories: Perceptual Understanding, Temporal Reasoning, and Anticipatory Assistance, along with StreamPro-F1 to evaluate response correctness, timing, and frequency. Experiments demonstrate that StreamPro substantially improves proactive streaming video understanding, achieving an average StreamPro-F1 of 32.8 on StreamPro-Bench, compared with 9.2 for the strongest baseline, while maintaining strong performance on real-time streaming tasks, reaching 79.8 on StreamingBench-RTVU.

中国人民大学.title: GeoScaffold: From Latent to Realized Geometry in Collaborative Detection
中国人民大学.authors_text: Kang Yang, Yance Fang, Gaochen Cui, Xiaoqiang Jin, Deying Li
中国人民大学.summary: GeoScaffold enhances collaborative 3D detection by introducing a training-only objective that improves localization accuracy in fused BEV features, significantly boosting detection performance.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Most collaborative 3D detectors fuse bird's-eye-view (BEV) features from connected vehicles and roadside infrastructure to aggregate complementary observations. Although modern communication, alignment, and fusion pipelines encode rich latent geometry in the fused BEV features, the standard readout pipeline inherited from single-agent detectors, i.e., anchor scoring, box decoding, and non-maximum suppression (NMS), does not fully exploit these geometric cues. We empirically identify and quantify this gap on UrbanIng-V2X. Collaboration improves localization at about two-thirds of positive anchors, yet when NMS resolves two overlapping collaborative boxes of one object, it keeps the better-localized box less than half of the time. A key cause is a supervision mismatch: classification scores are trained only for foreground-background discrimination, so nothing in training requires them to rank boxes by localization quality. To address this limitation, we introduce GeoScaffold, a lightweight training-only auxiliary objective. It predicts a foreground mask at each positive anchor, i.e., the cells of a grid over the anchor that lie inside the ground-truth box, to supply the dense spatial supervision that the seven-dimensional box code leaves implicit. Its loss, added to the detection loss, updates the encoder and fusion modules through the fused BEV and trains the detector toward a better-localized box at every positive anchor, including the top-scored one. The auxiliary head is removed at inference, preserving the original detector architecture, communication logic, and inference cost. GeoScaffold raises AP@0.5 and AP@0.7 by 0.98 and 0.55 points on average across all 11 fusion methods on the UrbanIng-V2X validation split, with gains extending to most methods on an unseen intersection and to all ten methods that produce detections on V2V4Real.

中国人民大学.title: MoHA: Model-Conditioned Harness Adaptation for Long-Video Agents
中国人民大学.authors_text: Jianghan Chao, Wenhui Tan, Hang Su, Qiuyu Tian, Tanxiao Li
中国人民大学.summary: MoHA introduces a framework for adapting execution harnesses in long-video agents, enhancing performance by optimizing planner-observer model coordination based on specific task needs.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Long-video understanding increasingly relies on agentic systems that actively acquire evidence rather than process fixed video representations. Their execution harnesses must coordinate language-level planning with video-level observation and evidence acquisition, yet are typically fixed across model stacks. We therefore introduce MoHA, a framework for model-conditioned harness adaptation that adapts a common initial execution harness to the specific planner and observer models it hosts. MoHA treats the harness itself as a model-conditioned optimization object: under the same task distribution and initialization, different planner-observer stacks can benefit from different executable harnesses. Starting from a common initial harness, MoHA analyzes failed calibration traces to diagnose model-harness mismatches and adapts both planner-side reasoning support, such as overview, memory, and verification, and observer-side capability assignments, including OCR and ASR specialists. After structural adaptation, MoHA separately calibrates observer execution configurations for the hosted model stack. Across three frozen planner stacks, MoHA improves Video-MME Full accuracy by 6.2-27.1 percentage points and Video-Holmes accuracy by 3.1-20.1 points over the fixed initial harness. Cross-model transfer further shows that the adapted harnesses generalize only partially to other models, highlighting the harness as a model-conditioned optimization layer for long-video understanding. Code is available at https://github.com/roverx12345/MoHA.

中国人民大学.title: Beyond Linear Decodability: Understanding and Improving Instruction Following in World Action Models
中国人民大学.authors_text: Bokai Ji, Jiapeng Chen, Yi Zhang, Zeyuan Ding, Yong Dai
中国人民大学.summary: This paper introduces linear decodability supervision (LDS) to enhance instruction-following in world action models, significantly improving performance and reconciling the role of encoded target information.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) exhibit strong manipulation capabilities yet often fail to follow test-time language instructions. Prior work shows that non-following (NF) WAMs encode information about the instructed target, but this information does not control their behavior. By comparing NF WAM with its instruction-following (IF) counterpart, we find that target information is substantially more linearly decodable in IF WAMs, despite being encoded in both. Motivated by this observation, we introduce linear decodability supervision (LDS), a simple yet effective auxiliary training objective that promotes the linear decodability of the instructed target information. On LIBERO-CF, InternW0-$Δ$ with LDS achieves a success rate of 74.6% and a grounding rate of 89.2%, surpassing the strongest baseline by 26.8 and 42.9 percentage points, respectively. The effectiveness of LDS challenges the prevailing interpretation that encoded target information does not contribute to WAMs' behavior. To reconcile this apparent contradiction, we propose a prior-instruction competition mechanism, which explains NF and IF behavior as arising from the dominance of prior and instruction signals, respectively. We provide causal evidence for this mechanism by evaluating two training-free interventions derived from it. We reinterpret LDS through this mechanism, showing that it acts as a form of instruction signal enhancement. Finally, more comprehensive evaluations across diverse manipulation tasks and visual domains demonstrate the consistent effectiveness of LDS.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: Simulation-Based Testing of RCM-Constrained Robotic Software via Task Manifolds
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Zhenyu Jiang, Yanlin Li, Rongjie Yan, Rihui Song, Kai Huang
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: This paper presents a manifold-centered testing framework for RCM-constrained robotic software, enhancing test efficiency and failure detection through feasible domain construction and diverse search strategies.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: System-level testing of surgical robots requires generating executable test scenarios that exercise diverse, safety-critical behaviors. However, remote-center-of-motion (RCM) surgical manipulators operate within tightly constrained workspaces governed by coupled task geometry, inverse kinematics, and motor limits. Direct sampling in motor-command or Cartesian spaces frequently wastes testing budgets on physically unfeasible configurations. To address this limitation, we present a manifold-centered testing framework that decouples feasible test-domain construction from downstream test-generation strategies. Candidate inputs are generated directly within this constructed feasible domain and mapped to lower-level joint commands for simulation execution. Offline trajectory safety oracles and a spatial reference grid then evaluate failure yield and coverage. We compare our task-manifold representation against Cartesian XYZ and principal component analysis (PCA) under random testing, systematic traversal, and genetic search strategies. Results demonstrate that the feasible task domain improves test-generation efficiency and enables systematic reference-cell coverage. Crucially, random and genetic search strategies detect a broader spectrum of failure patterns than baseline representations, revealing that complete reference-cell coverage alone does not exhaust intra-cell behavioral dynamics. Furthermore, differential testing between defective and patched controller versions reveals that targeted evolutionary search detects aggregate failure-rate shifts from software repairs. Finally, a cross-platform study on a 7-DoF Kinova Gen3 arm in MoveIt 2 confirms workflow transferability to kinematically redundant manipulators. Together, these findings highlight the necessity of combining feasibility-aware domain modeling with complementary search strategies for systematic testing of robot software.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: LexiconVLA: Learning Reusable Atomic Action Codebooks for Manipulation
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Zeming Wei, Jianheng Ye, Xinshuai Song, Sirui Chen, Yang Liu
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: LexiconVLA introduces a retrievable atomic-action lexicon for vision-language-action models, enhancing task performance and adaptability across manipulation tasks through trajectory reconstruction and visual alignment.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models struggle to reuse recurring atomic actions across manipulation tasks. Our diagnostic study reveals that reliable task completion does not imply consistent execution of constituent atomic actions across task contexts. We present LexiconVLA, a retrievable atomic-action lexicon for cross-task reuse. Global and detail codebooks capture shared interaction structure and fine-grained execution variation respectively, preserving both reusable patterns and execution details. Visual-Atomic Action Alignment couples trajectory reconstruction from visual state changes with visual outcome prediction from action codes, grounding the lexicon in motion and its effects. We learn these codebooks with trajectory reconstruction and visual alignment on our AtomAction Dataset of 57,803 segments from 69 tasks. A planner and scene-aware adapter translate new goals into code-conditioned subtasks for a shared policy, without skill-specific experts or deployment-time parameter updates. Across five policy backbones on 26 RLBench tasks, LexiconVLA largely maintains performance on 18 seen tasks while improving success on 8 tasks held out from policy training. With BridgeVLA, unseen-task success rises from 16.67% to 34.17% (+17.50 percentage points), and overall success reaches 71.08%, the highest among methods with reported results. Real-robot experiments demonstrate stepwise execution and failure recovery.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: PACE-WM: Parallel World Modeling with Action History for Visual Planning
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Haishan Liu, Shijie Lian, Bin Yu, Yao Zhang, Changti Wu
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: PACE-WM enhances visual planning by utilizing executed-action history for contextual future predictions, achieving 98% success and significantly faster planning compared to existing models.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: JEPA-style world models support visual planning by predicting future representations conditioned on future actions. However, similar observations can conceal different motion states, making temporal context essential for interpreting future action effects. We propose PACE-WM, a parallel world model that uses executed-action history to contextualize future prediction and planning. Specifically, PACE-WM maintains a recurrent memory of executed actions and uses this memory to condition a causal Transformer. PACE-WM predicts multiple future representations in parallel without recursive predicted-state feedback within each prediction window. We further introduce Reference-Anchored Minimum Progress (RAMP) for action selection during planning. RAMP scores candidate actions by their predicted goal improvement along direct and split paths relative to a shared reference. Across four visual planning tasks, PACE-WM with RAMP achieves an average success rate of $98\%$ and plans approximately $7$-$9\times$ faster than autoregressive LeWM under matched CEM settings. We also construct four controlled benchmarks to evaluate PACE-WM's capabilities in motion disambiguation, goal-relative motion, and goal adaptation. Project page is available at https://github.com/LHS180/PACE-WM.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Zunhai Su, Keyu Fan, Ruishan Guo, Zhongzhu Zhou, Jingzehua Xu
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: QuantStream3D introduces a novel KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers, achieving significant accuracy and efficiency improvements through geometry-guided mixed-precision techniques.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch. Quantization sensitivity varies across precision choices and cache locations, while perturbed retrieval changes geometry-head inputs and propagates through subsequent predictions and KV writes. Guided by these findings, we propose QuantStream3D, to our knowledge the first dedicated KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers. Geometry-Guided Mixed-Precision KV Quantization protects sensitive cross-view evidence, while Geometry-Aligned Quantization-Aware Distillation jointly adapts transformer blocks and geometry heads on student-generated quantized history. Across five benchmarks and two backbones, QuantStream3D achieves near-lossless geometric accuracy in most settings with predominantly 2-bit KV caches, and many configurations surpass unquantized inference. Compared with LLM-oriented KV quantizers, it reduces TUM absolute trajectory error and NeuralRGBD completeness error by up to 57.4% and 69.7%, respectively. Integration with existing native cache-pruning methods further pushes compression while improving reconstruction quality on NeuralRGBD. Our optimized StreamVGGT backend achieves $5.05\times$ physical KV compression and 23.1% lower latency at batch size one. Under a fixed memory budget on the same GPU, it supports $5.4\times$ the maximum batch size and up to $1.67\times$ the peak throughput of unquantized inference. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be made publicly available.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Ego4Gen: Generating Geometry-Grounded Motion Tokens as a World-Action Interface
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Yang Liu, Chao Ye, Jiahao Zhang, Zeyuan Hou, Ruijie Fang
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: Ego4Gen generates geometry-grounded motion tokens from egocentric images and text prompts, enabling improved robotic manipulation through 4D future prediction and reduced action-label dependency.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: We present Ego4Gen (Egocentric 4D Future Generation), a world model for 4D future generation in robotic manipu lation. Given a single egocentric image and a text prompt, Ego4Gen jointly generates temporally aligned RGB frames, dense point maps, and dense scene flow, explicitly pre dicting the evolution of scene appearance, spatial struc ture, and motion. Built on Cosmos3-Nano, Ego4Gen ex tends the pretrained generative backbone through modality routed LoRA and asymmetric attention, using geometric pseudo-labels from MotionCrafter to learn to predict future geometry and motion latents. These latents can either be decoded into explicit 3D structure and motion or mapped to robot actions. To this end, we also introduce FlowIn verse, a lightweight inverse dynamics network trained in two stages to translate predicted 4D latents into robot ac tions. Experiments show that these geometry and motion latents outperform the evaluated latent-action and video latent baselines in out-of-distribution settings. Closed loop policy evaluations further demonstrate their utility for translating predicted 4D futures into robot control. To gether, these results support geometry-grounded motion to kens as a world-action interface, connecting 4D future gen eration with robotic manipulation and suggesting a path to ward reduced reliance on action-labeled data.

天津大学.title: Towards Embodied Air-Ground Cooperative Object Search: Benchmark, Dataset and Agentic Method
天津大学.authors_text: Boao Yu, Zimo Chen, Junreng Rao, Yue Hu, Zhengqiu Zhu
天津大学.summary: The paper introduces AGOS-Bench, a benchmark for air-ground cooperative object search, presenting the AGOS-Dataset and AGOS-Agent, achieving notable success rates in urban environments.
天津大学.debug_abstract: Urban object search, locating a specific object from a single reference image without route or direction instructions and confirming the instance up close, is a fundamental capability for embodied agents. Existing urban embodied benchmarks evaluate one segment of this chain: navigation ends at a coordinate, and detection and question answering stop at an answer. We present AGOS-Bench, the first benchmark for urban cooperative object search by an air-ground team, integrating aerial discovery and ground-level instance verification in one closed loop. Nine metrics assess search, cooperation, and verification, and they distinguish "found but unconfirmed" from "never found". AGOS-Dataset instantiates the task in 2,125 episodes across six city maps under seen and unseen test settings, contributing 27,720 Train Examples along with 1,100 Expert Trajectories. To solve the task, we propose AGOS-Agent, which combines algorithmic coverage and approach routing with event-driven MLLM judgments for target verification and cooperation. On the unseen test set, zero-shot AGOS-Agent (Qwen3.5-4B) achieves a success rate (SR) of 37.67%, 7.00 percentage points (pp) above a controlled baseline with identical information, actions, and prompts. LoRA fine-tuning raises SR to 57.00% (+19.33 pp). Adapted existing systems AGC-VLN-OS and AeroDuo-OS achieve SRs of 31.33% and 28.67%, respectively. Project page: https://github.com/Yomier/AGOS-Bench.

具身智能研究中心.title: DIDO: Distilling Interaction-Centric Dynamics into One-Step Denoising for World Action Models
具身智能研究中心.authors_text: Jing Lyu, Shuanghao Bai, Runze Xiao, Zhenyu Liao, Wenxing Tan
具身智能研究中心.summary: DIDO distills multi-step video model dynamics into a single denoising step, enhancing robotic manipulation by preserving interaction-centric features and reducing latency, achieving high success rates across various tasks.
具身智能研究中心.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) use video generation models to predict future visual dynamics for robotic manipulation, but iterative denoising introduces additional latency for closed-loop control. We empirically find that visual content converges at different rates during denoising. Static background structure forms early, whereas the gripper and manipulated object remain blurry after the first step, with their interaction dynamics emerging only through subsequent denoising. Consequently, naively truncating a multi-step video model to one step preserves scene structure but loses the interaction-centric dynamics most critical for manipulation. To address this issue, we propose DIDO, which distills the converged dynamics of a multi-step video model into a single denoising step. DIDO combines distribution matching distillation with interaction-centric representation guidance. Beyond compressing multi-step generation into one forward pass, DIDO explicitly models the gripper, manipulated object, and their interaction using supervised bounding-box visual reasoning tokens. Additionally, DIDO aligns the target object's representations across multiple model layers with features from a pretrained DINOv3 encoder. This interaction-centric guidance helps the distilled model preserve both the relevant entities and their future dynamics in a single step, while substantially reducing inference latency. DIDO achieves an average success rate of 99.0\% on LIBERO, 76.6\% on LIBERO-Plus, and 92.0\% on RoboTwin, while also demonstrating effective transfer to long-horizon and generalization tasks in real-world robotic manipulation.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Jing Lyu, Shuanghao Bai, Runze Xiao, Zhenyu Liao, Wenxing Tan

CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.authors_text: Shengze Huang, Yanyu Mao, Xiaofei Yu, Baoshen Guo, Xiaorui Wang
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.summary: HookEvo is a framework that enhances tool-using agents by coordinating plugin evolution through lifecycle hooks, achieving significant performance improvements across various benchmarks.
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.debug_abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, the selected harnesses lead the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons, achieving 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench. Across three improvers and three edit scopes, from skill text to single-component and coordinated executable edits, GPT-6.1 Sol shows the largest average gain from the broadest scope. Our code is available at https://huangshengzebluesky.github.io/hookevo/.

CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.title: ProbeAgent: Principled Diagnosis of Agent Failures in Verifiable Environments
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.authors_text: Yue Huang, Yuchen Ma, Shuhang Lin, Yuyang Wu, Zixuan Weng
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.summary: ProbeAgent is an automated framework that diagnoses agent failures by identifying causes, testing hypotheses, and generating detailed descriptions of shared failure modes across multiple benchmarks.
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.debug_abstract: Improving agents requires discovering where they fail and understanding why. An agent acts over multiple steps in a changing environment, so diagnosing its failures requires more than inspecting the final response of a large language model (LLM). The same unsuccessful outcome can arise from task difficulty or from an error the agent repeats across tasks. We introduce ProbeAgent, an automated framework that discovers agent failures, tests their proposed causes, and identifies shared failure modes. Starting from benchmark tasks, ProbeAgent builds executable tests and validates them using reference solutions, automated checks, and review of the task requirements. For each failed trajectory, it explains the error and constructs new tasks that preserve the suspected cause while changing the surrounding context. Running the agent on these tasks tests whether the same error recurs. ProbeAgent then groups failures with similar causes and generates descriptions that distinguish their errors. This process connects explanations of individual failures to executable tests and descriptions of shared failure modes. We evaluate ProbeAgent across 22 agent configurations using tasks from 10 benchmarks, collecting 1,244 failures and producing 536 failure-mode descriptions. These descriptions distinguish specific errors within broad outcomes such as incomplete work, including planning without acting and stopping before delivering a file. In human evaluation, annotators accept 90.0% of assigned descriptions and correctly reject 83.3% of similar alternatives, supporting the accuracy and specificity of the discovered failure modes.

武汉大学.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
武汉大学.authors_text: Ziyi Ding, Yiwei Wang, Zhongxing Wei, Xianxin Lai, Yechi Liu
武汉大学.summary: EgoLAM enhances robot learning by using hand and head motion to decode latent actions from egocentric video, significantly outperforming existing models in task success rates.
武汉大学.debug_abstract: Latent action models let a robot policy learn from video by turning the change between two frames into a training target. In egocentric video, a cup can move across the image because a hand pushes it or because the wearer turns. Both changes help predict the next frame, but only the first describes manipulation. During training, EgoLAM supervises the action code with measured wrist motion and supplies camera motion separately to the forward model. Even when the wearer turns while pushing a cup, the training target still describes how the hand pushed it. The action encoder pools object slots around each hand, and wrist translation and rotation can be decoded from the code in a common reference frame. Extracting a code then requires only two RGB frames. Alongside LARYBench classification and regression, we measure how much wrist motion a frozen code retains and how strongly it responds to a synthetic view or lighting change. EgoLAM has the highest hand-motion decoding score among eight evaluated models. Across three LIBERO suites, policies pretrained on its codes and fine-tuned on expert demonstrations achieve 79.38% mean success, 28.73 points above expert behavior cloning and 9.76 points above the strongest other latent action model in each suite on average.

武汉大学.title: NavTTT: Adaptive Parametric Memory via Hierarchical Test-Time Training for Vision-and-Language Navigation
武汉大学.authors_text: Xiaoyu Luo, Chengxing Lin, Jiaxin Huang, Jiale Liu, Jingyu Guo
武汉大学.summary: NavTTT enhances vision-and-language navigation by introducing adaptive memory and hierarchical integration, improving long-term history retention and decision-making in dynamic environments.
武汉大学.debug_abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) demands that agents accumulate and reason over streaming visual observations throughout long navigation episodes. Existing approaches struggle to maintain long-term history, constrained by the finite context capacity of transformer architectures. To solve the problem, fast-weight test-time training (TTT) provides a mechanism for encoding streaming observations into an evolving parameter state. However, existing TTT does not distinguish informative observations from repetitive visual content, allowing redundant tokens to interfere with the retention of information needed for subsequent decisions. We propose Navigation-Conditioned Test-Time Training (NavTTT), which introduces adaptive memory formation and hierarchical memory integration for vision-and-language navigation. NavTTT leverages global navigation context to prioritize informative visual evidence and integrates language instructions with spatial information to construct spatially grounded memory representations. Episode-local nonlinear fast weights store these representations as Adaptive Parametric Memory (APM), preserving history beyond the visual context for later decisions. To reduce cross-layer coupling in memory formation, NavTTT maintains independent fast-weight memories across multiple decoder depths. This decoupled design prevents errors or biases from spreading across different memory levels. Meanwhile, it enables shared historical information to be independently represented at various levels of abstraction. Experiments demonstrate strong navigation performance on VLN-CE benchmarks and effective instruction following on a real robot.

厦门大学.title: HumanoidPose: Monocular 3D Pose Estimation for Humanoid Robots
厦门大学.authors_text: Jinlin Gan, Mingzhe Li, Junsheng Zhang, Zhibo Zhou, Jiahan Geng
厦门大学.summary: The paper introduces HumanoidPose, a framework and benchmark for monocular 3D pose estimation in humanoid robots, addressing gaps in existing pose estimation paradigms.
厦门大学.debug_abstract: As humanoid robots increasingly enter real-world environments, recovering their 3D whole-body pose from monocular imagery is becoming increasingly important for external state perception, motion analysis, and robot learning. However, Humanoid Robot Pose Estimation (HRPE) lies at the intersection of conventional Robot Pose Estimation (RPE) and Human Pose Estimation (HPE), while not being fully addressed by either paradigm: RPE primarily focuses on non-humanoid robots, particularly fixed-base manipulators, whereas HPE is built upon human-specific skeletal topologies, body models, and motion priors. Despite recent progress in humanoid 2D keypoint detection and HPE adaptation, humanoid-native 3D pose recovery remains insufficiently studied, and a dedicated benchmark with suitable training data and evaluation protocols is still lacking. To address this gap, we introduce Humanoids, a benchmark for monocular 3D humanoid robot pose estimation, and propose HumanoidPose, a framework for this task. Humanoids provides synthetic 3D supervision across diverse humanoid embodiments, manually annotated real-world 2D data, and real-world RGB sequences paired with robot states for 3D evaluation on a physical Roban humanoid. HumanoidPose combines human-inspired visual perception with robot articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding. Experiments on Humanoids and the DHRP-H1 benchmark demonstrate strong performance in articulation recovery and 3D pose estimation, including zero-shot transfer to real-world 2D and 3D evaluation. Ablation studies further show the contribution of robot-native articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding. The dataset and code will be publicly released to support future research in the community.
